narration.text: Businesses owe each other in circles. A roaster owes its packaging supplier, who owes a freight firm, who owes the cafe that buys the roaster’s beans. Paid one by one, four hundred dollars moves. Yet the debts cancel out.
Wall Street solved this long ago. On an average day in 2020, DTCC netted $1.77 trillion of trades down to $38 billion. About 98% never had to move.
Small businesses still pay every invoice in full.
Quits is a clearing house for invoices, on Arc.
This is Arc mainnet. Seven companies, twenty invoices, $74.66 of debt. One netting cycle cleared all of it by moving fifteen cents.

Companies issue invoices and debtors accept them. Each keeps a small USDC deposit. Anyone computes the netting in the browser, and one atomic transaction settles it, with every rule re-checked on chain.

Arc makes it natural. USDC is the native coin, so a deposit is one transaction with no approval. Finality is deterministic: a settled cycle is final in under a second. Circle’s blocklist is enforced in the clearing rules. Invoices carry references through Arc’s Memo, batches go through Multicall3From, and a whole cycle costs about a cent.
Netting is only fair if nobody can cherry-pick. Quits draws cash only from members who sent the cycle, or approved whoever did. Pure loops of debt clear for anyone.
No owner, no admin, no fees. 176 tests and seven invariants stand behind the contract, and its source is verified on Sourcify and on Arc’s explorer.
Quits. Call it quits on circular debt.
